title: Spicy Arrabbiata Spaghetti
summary: From-scratch spicy red sauce built on chiles bloomed in oil and fried tomato paste, with the pasta finished in the pan.

ingredients.note: or 2 to 3 tbsp Calabrian chili paste
only if still sharp after butter

steps.title: Soften the onion
steps.text: Cook the onion in the olive oil until soft.

steps.title: Bloom garlic and chile
steps.text: Add the garlic and chile over medium-low until the garlic is pale gold. Brown garlic turns bitter.

steps.title: Fry the paste
steps.text: Add the tomato paste and fry until it darkens to brick red.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Add the tomatoes, salt, and rind. Simmer uncovered until thick and glossy.

steps.title: Fix the acid
steps.text: Taste. If it's sharp, stir in the butter first. Still sharp, add a pinch of baking soda, let the foam settle, and taste before adding more. More sugar won't fix it.

steps.title: Cook the pasta
steps.text: Boil the spaghetti in well-salted water, pulling it 2 minutes before done. Save the pasta water.

steps.title: Finish in the sauce
steps.text: Move the pasta into the sauce with about a cup of pasta water and toss over medium-high for 2 minutes until the sauce clings. Do it in two batches for this much pasta.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Off the heat, toss with parsley and serve with Parmesan.

notes: First batch came out acidic even with San Marzanos; cans vary, and many aren't certified DOP. Sugar didn't fix it. Butter first, then baking soda a pinch at a time. Parmesan and pasta water round it out too, so aim for slightly bright in the pot.
